steps: Boil the potatoes and mash them. Let cool completely — warm potatoes absorb oil and the patties won't hold together.
Mix the mash with the eggs, crumbled feta, spring onions, parsley, flour, salt, and pepper.
Shape into small round patties.
Heat the oil over medium-high heat.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until well browned.
Serve with tzatziki.
Preparation: Wash the potatoes well and put them whole, unpeeled, into a pot with plenty of cold water and a little salt.

Boiling: Boil the potatoes for about 25-30 minutes, depending on size. Important: boil them whole with the skin on so they don't absorb too much water and become soggy. They're ready when a fork slides in easily but they don't fall apart.
Peeling: Drain the potatoes and, while still warm but cool enough to handle, peel off the skins.
Cutting: Cut the potatoes into thick slices or large chunks and transfer them to a large salad bowl while still warm, so they absorb the dressing better.
Dressing: In a bowl, whisk together the olive oil, vinegar or lemon juice, mustard, oregano, salt, and pepper with a fork until combined.
Mixing: Finely chop the onion and parsley, add them to the potatoes along with the dressing, and toss gently so the potatoes don't break apart.
Resting: Let the salad rest for at least 15-20 minutes for the flavors to come together. Serve warm or at room temperature, with an extra drizzle of olive oil.
patatosalata.plate: Serve warm on a shallow plate, sprinkled with fresh parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.

steps: Cleaning the tripe: Important: Wash the tripe repeatedly under running water and scrub it with coarse salt and vinegar. This step decides everything — badly cleaned tripe gives an unpleasant smell no amount of cooking will fix.
Blanching: Boil it for 10 minutes in plenty of water, drain it and rinse it, discarding that first water entirely.
Cutting: Cut the blanched tripe into strips about 3 cm wide.
Boiling: Cover with fresh water, add the trotter, the bay leaves and the peppercorns and simmer for 3 hours.
Skimming: Skim the foam off the surface for the first 20 minutes, so the broth stays clear rather than cloudy.
Testing: The tripe is ready when it is completely soft and gelatinous and a piece tears easily between your fingers.
Straining: Strain the broth and keep about 1.5 litres of it — this is the soul of the dish.
Making the roux: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, then whisk in hot broth gradually so no lumps form.
Making the avgolemono: Beat the eggs with the lemon juice, then temper them slowly with hot broth, one ladle at a time, beating constantly. Important: rushing this curdles the eggs instantly.
Combining: Pour the avgolemono back into the pot, stir gently and never let it boil again.
Serving: Serve with a garlic and vinegar sauce (skordostoumbi) and chilli flakes on the table for everyone to season their own bowl.
patsas.wine: Traditionally none — patsas goes with tsipouro or plain water.
patsas.plate: Serve steaming hot in a deep bowl, with vinegar-garlic and chilli flakes on the side.

steps: Preheating: Preheat the oven to 120°C (fan) and line a tray with parchment paper, drawing a 20 cm circle on it as a guide.
Whisking the egg whites: Whisk the egg whites in a clean, dry bowl with a mixer at medium speed until frothy and forming soft peaks.
Adding the sugar: Add the sugar gradually, one tablespoon at a time, whisking continuously at high speed until the meringue is glossy and thick.
Important: The meringue is ready when, rubbing a little between your fingers, you feel no sugar granules; otherwise the pavlova will 'weep' syrup during baking.
Folding in: Carefully fold in the cornstarch, lemon juice and vanilla with a spatula, using gentle bottom-to-top motions so the meringue doesn't lose volume.
Shaping: Spread the meringue within the drawn circle, creating a slight hollow in the center to hold the filling later.
Baking: Bake for 75-90 minutes without opening the oven door, until the surface is hard and crisp. Turn off the oven and let the meringue cool completely inside with the door ajar.
Whipped cream: Whip the heavy cream with the powdered sugar until it thickens slightly, without becoming too stiff.
Assembly: Spread the whipped cream on the cooled meringue base and garnish generously with strawberries, kiwi and passion fruit pulp just before serving.
pavlova.plate: Serve on a flat platter, cut into slices, with an extra spoonful of fresh seasonal fruit

steps: Whisking the liquids: Whisk the olive oil with the sugar and the orange juice until they emulsify and thicken slightly.
Adding the eggs: Beat in the eggs, keeping one yolk aside for brushing.
Making the dough: Add the sifted flour with the baking powder and the spices, mixing to a firm, pliable dough.
Kneading: Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Important: unlike koulourakia, paximadakia want a well-kneaded dough — they need to hold together through two bakings.
Shaping the logs: Form long logs about 6 cm wide and flatten them slightly on the tray.
Brushing: Brush with the reserved yolk and press sesame seeds all over the surface.
First bake: Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes, until firm and golden.
Important: Take them out and let them cool for 15 minutes before slicing. Hot logs crumble under the knife; cooled ones cut cleanly.
Slicing: Cut into slices about 1.5 cm thick with a serrated knife, using a sawing motion.
Second bake: Lay the slices cut-side up and bake again at 150°C for 25-30 minutes, until completely dry. This second low bake is what makes them keep for weeks.
paximadakia_elaioladou.plate: Serve in a basket or glass jar — they keep for weeks.

steps: Preparing the aromatics: Cut the 4 garlic cloves into thin slices and finely chop the 1-2 hot chili peppers. Thin garlic slices release aroma without burning easily.

Sautéing: In 4 tbsp olive oil over medium heat, sauté the garlic and chili for about 2 minutes, until fragrant. IMPORTANT: be careful not to burn the garlic, as it turns bitter and ruins the whole sauce.
Sauce: Add the 400g grated tomato and a little salt. Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, until it thickens, turns glossy, and loses its raw acidity.
Boiling the pasta: In plenty of boiling salted water, cook the 200g penne al dente, meaning slightly firm, 1-2 minutes less than the package instructions. It will finish cooking in the sauce.
Cooking water: Before draining, reserve a cup of the starchy cooking water. This water binds the sauce to the pasta and helps it become velvety.
Tossing: Add the penne to the sauce along with a little cooking water and stir for 1-2 minutes over high heat so it's well coated. Add fresh basil.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, and sprinkle with Parmesan if desired. Arrabbiata-style pasta is best eaten freshly made, so the sauce doesn't dry out.
Cutting the zucchini: Cut the 3 zucchini (400g) into rounds or small cubes. Pat them lightly dry so they brown rather than steam in the pan.

Browning the zucchini: Brown the zucchini in 20g butter for 5-6 minutes until golden. IMPORTANT: don't stir constantly — let them sit in the hot butter to caramelize, which gives the sauce sweetness and depth.
Garlic: Add the 2 finely chopped garlic cloves and sauté for just 1 minute until fragrant — no longer, as garlic burns easily in butter and turns bitter.
Creamy sauce: Add the 150ml heavy cream, salt and pepper and simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly. The cream coats the zucchini and creates a velvety texture.
Cooking the pasta: Boil the 200g penne al dente, meaning slightly firm. IMPORTANT: reserve a little pasta water — its starch helps the sauce cling to the penne and makes them tastier.
Combining and serving: Add the penne to the sauce with a little pasta water and stir over low heat until combined. Add the 50g parmesan and fresh basil or mint, and serve immediately.
Preparing the chicken: Cut the chicken breast into small cubes or strips and season with salt and pepper.
Sautéing the chicken: In a large pan, heat the olive oil over high heat and sauté the chicken until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.

Mushrooms: In the same pan, add the chopped onion and garlic and sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened, then add the sliced mushrooms. Important: Don't stir the mushrooms constantly at first; let them sit undisturbed for a few minutes so they caramelize and release their liquid instead of just boiling.
Deglazing with wine: Deglaze with the white wine and let the alcohol evaporate over high heat for 2 minutes.
Pasta: Meanwhile, boil the penne in plenty of salted water until al dente, according to the package instructions, reserving a cup of the cooking water.
Combining the ingredients: Return the chicken to the pan with the mushrooms, add the heavy cream and simmer for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Finishing: Drain the penne and add them to the pan, mixing well with the sauce, adding a little of the cooking water if needed for a creamier texture. Add the Parmesan and stir until melted.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, sprinkled with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan.
pennes_kotopoulo_manitaria.wine: White Assyrtiko wine or a light Chardonnay pair excellently with the creamy sauce.
pennes_kotopoulo_manitaria.plate: Serve in a deep plate with grated Parmesan and fresh parsley on top, accompanied by fresh bread.

steps: Lightly toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Put the basil, pine nuts, parmesan, garlic and salt in a blender.
Blend, gradually adding the olive oil, until it becomes a smooth paste.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Store in a jar with a little oil on top in the fridge.
Sautéing the vegetables: Heat the olive oil in a wide pot. Sauté the onion for 3 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute. Add the diced carrot, zucchini and bell pepper, and sauté for 4-5 minutes.
Rice: Add the rice and sauté for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells lightly nutty.
Cooking: Add the tomato, stock, turmeric, thyme and salt. Stir and bring to a boil. Important: immediately lower the heat, cover, and cook for 15-18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Finishing: Remove from the heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Serve with fresh herbs.
pilafi_laxanikon.plate: With fresh parsley and grated feta.

steps: Roll out the dough and spread with a little tomato sauce.
Distribute the 4 cheeses evenly.
Bake at 250°C for 12-14 minutes until the cheeses melt and turn golden.
Garnish with basil and serve.
Dough: Roll out the dough on a round baking sheet or pizza stone to a thickness of 0.5 cm.
Sauce: Spread the tomato sauce evenly, leaving a 1 cm border for the crust.
Mushrooms: Lightly sauté the mushrooms in a little olive oil before adding them to the pizza, so they don't release water during baking.
Toppings: Spread the mozzarella, then the ham, mushrooms, artichokes halved, and olives.
Important: The oven must be preheated to 250°C for at least 20 minutes beforehand, ideally with a pizza stone, so the dough bakes quickly and stays crisp without the toppings drying out.
Baking: Bake on the lowest rack of the oven for 10-12 minutes, until the crust is well browned.
Drizzling: As soon as it comes out of the oven, drizzle with a thread of olive oil.
Serving: Sprinkle with oregano and cut into slices immediately.
pizza_capricciosa.plate: Serve whole on a wooden board, cut into slices.

steps: Fry the bacon with a little garlic until crisp.
Beat the eggs with the cream and parmesan.
Roll out the dough and spread with the egg-and-cream mixture.
Top with mozzarella and the bacon.
Bake at 230°C for 13-15 minutes.
Grind fresh pepper on top and serve immediately.
Dough: Roll the dough out thin on a round baking sheet or pizza stone.
Sauce: Mix the tomato sauce with the finely chopped garlic and spread it evenly.
Cheese: Add the mozzarella in pieces over the whole surface.
Salami: Arrange the spicy salami slices evenly over the pizza.
Important: Use piccante (spicy) salami rather than plain salami, as this gives the characteristic hot 'diavola' flavor during baking, letting its fat render and melt over the cheese.
Baking: Bake at 250°C for 10-12 minutes, until the salami sizzles lightly at the edges.
Heat: Sprinkle with hot pepper flakes as soon as it comes out of the oven.
Serving: Drizzle with olive oil and serve immediately while hot.
pizza_diavola.plate: On a wooden board, cut into slices, with extra pepper flakes on the side.

steps: Cut the chicken into strips and marinate with mustard, paprika, salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken in a pan until done.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella, chicken, peppers and onion.
Bake at 250°C for 13-15 minutes.
Serve hot.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, salt, olive oil and the yeast water. Knead for 8-10 minutes.
Let the dough rise, covered, for 1 hour.
Roll out the dough into a round base. Spread with tomato sauce.
Top with pieces of mozzarella.
Bake at 250°C for 12-15 minutes until golden.
Remove from the oven, top with fresh basil and serve immediately.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella and pepperoni slices.
Bake at 250°C for 12-14 minutes until golden.
Sprinkle with oregano and chili flakes if desired.
Serve immediately.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella, sliced mushrooms and olives.
Bake at 250°C for 12 minutes.
Remove from the oven and add the prosciutto on top.
Sprinkle with oregano and serve.
Dough: Roll the dough out thin on a round baking sheet or pizza stone.
Sauce: Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce over the surface.
Cheese: Add the mozzarella in pieces, evenly distributed.
Important: Prosciutto crudo is NEVER baked with the pizza, as it toughens and loses its flavor; it is always added raw after baking.
Baking: Bake at 250°C for 8-10 minutes, until the dough is golden and the cheese has melted well.
Arugula: Toss the arugula with a little olive oil and lemon juice in a bowl.
Serving: As soon as the pizza comes out of the oven, arrange the prosciutto slices and arugula on top.
Finishing: Sprinkle with Parmesan shavings and a final drizzle of olive oil.
pizza_prosciutto_rucola.plate: On a wooden board, cut into diagonal slices.

steps: Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella and distribute all the toppings evenly.
Bake at 250°C for 13-15 minutes until golden.
Sprinkle with oregano and serve hot.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce and mozzarella.
Mentally divide the pizza into 4 sections.
In each section, place one of the 4 toppings: ham, mushrooms, artichokes, olives.
Bake at 250°C for 13-15 minutes.
Sprinkle with oregano and serve.
Cut the vegetables into thin slices. Lightly sauté in a pan with a little oil.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella and the vegetables.
Sprinkle with oregano and a little olive oil.
Bake at 250°C for 13-15 minutes.
Serve hot.
Cut the cabbage into thin strips and the carrots into matchsticks.
Finely chop the pepper and celery.
Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar and salt.
Toss all the vegetables with the dressing.
Let marinate for 30 minutes before serving.

Drying the filo: Unroll the filo sheets and spread them out crumpled on a baking sheet or countertop for 2-3 hours, so they dry out well and become crisp. Important: Well-dried filo is the secret to authentic orange pie, as it absorbs the syrup properly and gives the characteristic spongy texture without turning soggy.
Crumbling: Crumble the dried filo by hand into small pieces in a large bowl.
Batter: In another bowl, beat the eggs with the sugar until fluffy, add the sunflower oil, the yogurt, the orange zest, and finally the baking powder. Mix until smooth.
Combining: Pour the wet batter over the crumbled filo and stir gently until fully absorbed and all the pieces are soaked.
Baking: Butter a baking pan, pour in the mixture and bake in a preheated oven at 170°C for about 40-45 minutes, until the top turns golden.
Syrup: While the pie bakes, boil the water with the sugar and orange juice for 5-7 minutes until it thickens slightly. Remove from heat and let cool to lukewarm.
Syruping: Important: Always pour a hot dessert with lukewarm syrup (or vice versa), never hot with hot, so it absorbs evenly and stays syrupy without turning soggy.
Resting: Let the orange pie absorb all the syrup for at least 2-3 hours before cutting it into pieces and serving.
portokalopita.wine: Sour cherry cordial or a sweet white wine.
portokalopita.plate: Serve cold with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and a little orange zest.
